gold_rationale: Specific, testable behavior: position is either displayed or it is not. Update rate is handled separately by REQ-002.
Model requirement. Quantified threshold (500 ms) plus explicit operating modes. Use as a positive exemplar in the taxonomy.
Clear capability, directly testable.
Both 'safe' and 'efficient' are undefined. SWEHB names 'efficient' explicitly as a subjective term to avoid. SRS Open Items #1 confirms 'safe route' is unresolved.
Trigger condition and action both stated.
'reasonably close' has no numeric tolerance, so no acceptance criterion can be written. Open Items #2 confirms.
'continuously monitor' specifies no sampling rate or staleness bound. A 1 Hz and a 1000 Hz implementation both satisfy the wording.
notes: Judgment call: 'continuously' could be read as clear enough.

gold_rationale: Exemplary: quantified threshold tied to a defined quantity (usable fuel capacity).
Threshold and both outputs are unambiguous and testable. Noted as compound only because two obligations share one ID, which affects verification tracking rather than clarity.
notes: Several obligations under one ID; not treated as a defect (Mark's issue codes have no compound category).

gold_rationale: The trigger (engine failure) is defined but the required response is not. 'Appropriate corrective action' delegates a flight-safety design decision to the developer.
Testable given a defined sensor range.
Clear capability.
Enumerated list is complete and each field is testable. Compound only in the traceability sense - four display fields under one ID.
notes: Several obligations under one ID; not treated as a defect (Mark's issue codes have no compound category).

gold_rationale: Safety-critical inhibit, clearly stated and testable.

'Friendly' is never defined, and SRS Open Items #10 admits friend-or-foe criteria are unresolved, so this safety inhibit can't be implemented or verified as written. Its precedence over REQ-035's pilot override also needs clarification.

gold_rationale: 'Extremely accurate' has no metric or units. Open Items #7 confirms targeting accuracy is unresolved. Separately, the subject is 'the targeting system', not the SFMC - this may not be a software requirement at all.
notes: Also ALLOCATION_UNCLEAR: the subject is 'the targeting system', not the SFMC.

gold_rationale: Trigger and response both stated. No latency bound, but REQ-021 is where that gap is recorded.
'Clearly indicate' is subjective, and 'greatest danger' implies a threat-ranking function with no stated criteria (closure rate? weapon type? time to impact?).
Mode-triggered action, testable.
Condition and action stated; 'when automatic defense is enabled' is a clear precondition.
Both 'quickly' and 'dangerous' are undefined, and 'respond' does not name an action. Three separate gaps in one sentence.
Clear capability.
Trigger and response stated.
Clear capability.

'Important' is undefined (Open Items #4) and 'securely encrypted' names no algorithm or standard. Also written in passive voice with no subject, so it is unclear the SFMC is the responsible component.
notes: Also ALLOCATION_UNCLEAR: passive voice with no responsible component.

gold_rationale: Enumerated scope, testable.
Model requirement: trigger, response, and a 1-second latency bound.
Clear obligation.
Complete enumeration of required fields; each is testable.
notes: Several obligations under one ID; not treated as a defect (Mark's issue codes have no compound category).

gold_rationale: 'Critical' is undefined (Open Items #3) and 'immediately' has no time bound. It also overlaps REQ-027, which bounds fault display at 1 second, without saying which applies to critical faults.
notes: Rationale corrected: overlap with REQ-027, not a conflict.

gold_rationale: Testable. Subject is the pilot rather than the SFMC, which is a minor style inconsistency, not a defect.

'Prioritize' names no mechanism (CPU scheduling? function shedding?) and 'nonessential' is undefined. Separately, life-support is NOT listed as an SFMC-connected subsystem in SRS section 1.2, so this requirement references a system the SFMC is not documented to control.
notes: Also ALLOCATION_UNCLEAR: life-support is not an SFMC-connected subsystem in §1.2.

gold_rationale: 'Seriously damaged' and 'safest destination' are both undefined. Open Items #5 confirms 'safe location' is unresolved.

'Safe location' undefined (Open Items #5). 'Shall be capable of' states a capability rather than a behavior, which is weaker than 'shall fly'. Also overlaps REQ-033 and REQ-005 without stating how they interact.
'Always' is broad, and the SRS doesn't say whether pilot override extends to safety inhibits such as REQ-015's friendly-fire block. Needs clarification; the text alone doesn't prove a contradiction.
notes: Corrected: the Weeks 1-2 review called this a direct conflict with REQ-015.

gold_rationale: Quantified (30 s) and testable. 'Operational' is not formally defined, but boot-to-ready is a reasonable reading.
'Without noticeable delay' is subjective and observer-dependent. Open Items #8 confirms.

The 10 Hz minimum is testable, but 'normal operation' isn't one of the SRS's defined modes and 'flight information' isn't defined, so it's unclear when and to what it applies. It is compatible with REQ-002: both set minimum rates.
notes: Judgment call (could be ACCEPTABLE). Corrected: the Weeks 1-2 review called this a conflict with REQ-002.

gold_rationale: Quantified duration, testable.
'Never crash' is a universal negative and cannot be demonstrated by finite testing. Reliability must be expressed statistically or against a defined operational profile.
'Recoverable' is defined only by the fact that recovery is possible, making the requirement circular. No recovery time bound is given either.
notes: Circular: 'recoverable' is defined only by the fact that recovery succeeds.

gold_rationale: 'Important mission data' is undefined. Same undefined qualifier as REQ-025, applied to a different subsystem.
'Whenever possible' makes the requirement unfalsifiable - any failure to continue operating can be attributed to it not being possible.
Clear obligation; contents are specified in REQ-045.
Complete enumeration of six event classes, each individually testable. Compound in the traceability sense only.
notes: Several obligations under one ID; not treated as a defect (Mark's issue codes have no compound category).

gold_rationale: Clear and testable.
'Sufficient storage' gives no capacity figure and no worst-case event rate to derive one from. Open Items #6 confirms.
Clear precondition on spacecraft operation, testable.
Testable given a defined authorization scheme; REQ-048 provides adjacent context.
'State-of-the-art' names no standard and changes meaning over time, so the same implementation could pass today and fail later. Open Items #9 confirms.
Legitimate design constraint, clearly stated.
Legitimate interface constraint.
Testable, with a clear mode precondition. Subject is maintenance personnel rather than the SFMC - minor style inconsistency only.
Clear obligation with a defined ordering ('before installing').

REQ-035 lets the pilot always override automatic controls; REQ-015 forbids firing at friendly spacecraft. The SRS doesn't say whether the weapons inhibit is an overridable automatic control, so precedence needs clarifying. The text alone doesn't prove a contradiction.
notes: Corrected: the Weeks 1-2 review called this a direct conflict.

gold_rationale: Both are minimums: updating at least 10 times per second also satisfies at least once every 500 ms. Scope may be unclear, but both can be met together.
notes: Corrected: the Weeks 1-2 review called this a conflict.

gold_rationale: Both describe automatic emergency navigation, but with different triggers ('seriously damaged' vs 'during an emergency') and targets ('safest destination' vs 'a safe location'). The SRS doesn't say whether REQ-034 flies to the destination REQ-033 chooses. They can coexist, so this is not a conflict.
notes: Judgment call.

gold_rationale: Section 10 lists ten parent mission needs but says the requirement-to-need traceability matrix hasn't been developed, so no requirement is linked to a parent.
notes: Criterion: TRACEABILITY.

gold_rationale: No section states how the requirements will be verified. Handbook 5.09 recommends qualification provisions naming Demonstration, Testing, Analysis or Inspection. A Handbook guidance gap, not an NPR violation.
notes: Criterion inferred from scope: QUALIFICATION_PROVISIONS.

gold_rationale: None of the 54 requirements in sections 3-9 states acceptance criteria or rationale, which the Handbook's structured requirement format recommends. Some are quantified enough to test, but none says how acceptance is judged.
notes: Criterion inferred from scope: ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA. Judgment call: could be PARTIAL, since some requirements are testable as written.

gold_rationale: Section 2.1 contains two 'shall' statements (receive pilot commands; display status on the primary display) with no requirement ID, while every requirement in sections 3-9 is numbered. It's unclear whether they are binding.
notes: Criterion inferred from scope: REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIERS.

gold_rationale: Safety-relevant requirements exist (weapons inhibits REQ-014/015, emergency operation REQ-031 to 035), but the terms they depend on are undefined: friend-or-foe criteria, 'safe location', 'seriously damaged'. Section 11 lists several as open items.
notes: Criterion inferred from scope: SAFETY_DEFINITIONS.

gold_rationale: The SRS itself shows requirements are captured and recorded (numbered, sectioned, versioned), but approval and ongoing maintenance can't be established from an SRS; its status is 'Draft for Review'.
notes: The Weeks 1-2 analysis treated SWE-050 as process-only; this counts the SRS as evidence of capture and recording.

gold_rationale: Parent mission needs are listed (section 10), which shows some flow-down, but there are no requirement-to-parent links and no reference to safety or reliability analyses or hardware specifications. The analysis itself needs external evidence.
notes: Judgment call: could be NOT_ASSESSABLE, since requirements analysis is a process.

gold_rationale: Some safety controls are documented (weapons authorization and friendly-fire inhibits, emergency mode), but key safety terms are undefined and there is no hardware/operator/software safety-constraint section, so completeness can't be verified.
Tracking and managing changes is a process. A version number doesn't show change control; this needs change requests and configuration management records.

Identifying inconsistencies, taking corrective action and tracking to closure is a process. The SRS shows interactions that need clarification (REQ-015/035, REQ-033/034) and an open-items list (section 11), but not whether they were tracked to closure; this needs an issue log.
notes: Judgment call: the section 11 open-items list is related, but it covers undefined terms rather than inconsistencies.

gold_rationale: Validating that the software will perform as intended in the customer environment needs stakeholder review or validation records, not the SRS text.
